title: Zampogna
summary: The zampogna is an Italian bagpipe of the central and southern regions, with a bag of sheep or goat skin and two chanters, one for the melody and one for the accompaniment, with drones beside them. The pipes end in curved horn bells and hang from the stock below the bag.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. The chanter is the pipe with the finger holes.
The bag gives each time a note sounds, and the drones keep the home note.
Strike close to the beat; a repeated note is cut with a quick grace note.
rules: Seven notes of the chanter, each struck close to its beat.
The drone sounds from the first breath to the last: the notes sit on top of it.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Pipers have played it for generations at winter festivals and in the hills; the melody sits on top of the drone while the bag is pressed by the arm.
credits: Tradition: the zampogna; melodies written for this game
